creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Filed by Quartermaster's orchestrator (an agent), not the owner, from Quartermaster's agent interface work on 2026-10-17.

While a pane's agent waits in a `qm run` that Quartermaster has queued, the pane reads `working` and nobody can see why it is not progressing. Quartermaster knows: every job carries the pane it came from, `session = "muster:<pane id>"` (from `MUSTER_PANE`).

The contract (Quartermaster's main, 2026-10-17; `qm docs queue`): `qm queue --json` lists each machine's waiting jobs with `job_id`, `session`, `position`, `rule` (such as `cores-short`) and `reason` (one sentence, such as "wants 4 cores, starts with at least 2; 1 free"); it exits 3 when no daemon answers. A `qm run` whose `--wait-at-most` runs out exits 75 with its place held for 2 minutes and prints `qm: still waiting after ...` on stderr.

Quartermaster works without Muster, so Muster pulls: for example, while a pane is `working` and its process tree holds a `qm run`, call `qm queue --json` and show the waiting job whose `session` matches, such as "queued: next in line (cores-short)". How often to ask, and whether to read the daemon's socket directly instead, is Muster's call. A `qm queue --session <tag>` filter is on Quartermaster's board if asking per pane matters.
title: Show a queued qm run's reason in its pane's waiting state
